records.title: Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories
inspected_sections: Main narrative sections 1–5, appendices A/B and experimental tables 1–5. Displayed formula proofs and every referenced work were not independently reproduced.

claims_supported: Memory consolidation expands or activates low-rank experts and transfers knowledge through generalized on-policy distillation plus reinforcement-learning imitation.
Dreaming combines random expert activation, synthetic examples, gradient-based selection and trained model adaptations.
Appendix B.2 uses task-finetuned small models for the 10-million-token BABILong result and reports substantial drops without fine-tuning.
The ARC evaluation uses 11 filtered training tasks and eight held-out tasks and reports successful-dream fractions. Mathematical scores use average@16.
Appendix B.5 reports that same-step SFT is four times more efficient, with different conclusions under selected comparisons of time to reach a performance target.
application: Inspire an explicitly nonparametric, source-bound consolidation experiment that preserves original sources, qualifications and regression checks.
limitations: Our source-card/index experiment does not update model weights or reproduce this paper.

The authors’ experimental results are not local performance measurements or proof of unlimited continual learning.
